chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.topic: 1H NMR chemical shift of aromatic protons
questions.question: In 1H NMR spectroscopy, where do benzene ring protons typically absorb?

options.label: C
options.text: δ 6.5 to 8.5 ppm due to magnetic anisotropy from the aromatic ring current

questions.correct_answer: δ 6.5 to 8.5 ppm due to magnetic anisotropy from the aromatic ring current
questions.explanation: The induced magnetic field of circulating pi electrons strongly deshields aromatic protons outside the ring.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What splitting pattern and integration ratio characterizes an isolated ethyl group (-CH2CH3)?
questions.correct_answer: Triplet (3H) and Quartet (2H)
questions.explanation: According to the n+1 rule, 3 methyl protons split CH2 into a quartet; 2 methylene protons split CH3 into a triplet.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What splitting pattern in 1H NMR identifies an isopropyl group (-CH(CH3)2)?
questions.correct_answer: Doublet (6H) and Septet (1H)
questions.explanation: The single methine proton splits the 6 equivalent methyl hydrogens into a doublet; methyls split methine into a septet.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What signal in 1H NMR characterizes an isolated tert-butyl group (-C(CH3)3)?

options.label: C
options.text: A sharp 9-proton singlet near δ 0.9 to 1.3 ppm

questions.correct_answer: A sharp 9-proton singlet near δ 0.9 to 1.3 ppm
questions.explanation: All 9 protons in a tert-butyl group are chemically equivalent with no neighboring protons, appearing as a 9H singlet.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Where does an aldehyde formyl proton (R-CHO) appear in a 1H NMR spectrum?

options.label: B
options.text: δ 9.0 to 10.0 ppm as a distinctive downfield singlet/doublet

questions.correct_answer: δ 9.0 to 10.0 ppm as a distinctive downfield singlet/doublet
questions.explanation: Anisotropic deshielding and carbonyl electronegativity shift aldehyde protons far downfield.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.topic: 13C NMR signal count in symmetrical molecules
questions.question: How many signals appear in the broad-band decoupled 13C NMR spectrum of 1,4-dichlorobenzene?

options.label: C
options.text: 2 signals (1 for the two C-Cl carbons, 1 for the four C-H carbons)

questions.correct_answer: 2 signals (1 for the two C-Cl carbons, 1 for the four C-H carbons)
questions.explanation: Planes of symmetry make carbons equivalent: 2 identical quaternary carbons and 4 identical C-H carbons.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: In a DEPT-135 13C NMR spectrum, how do methylene (-CH2-) carbons appear?

options.label: B
options.text: Negative signals pointing downward below the baseline

questions.correct_answer: Negative signals pointing downward below the baseline
questions.explanation: DEPT-135 selectively displays CH3 and CH carbons positive (up) and CH2 carbons negative (down).

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: How can quaternary carbons (carbons with no attached hydrogens) be identified using DEPT NMR?

options.label: A
options.text: They appear in normal 13C broad-band decoupled spectra but disappear in all DEPT spectra (DEPT-45, 90, 135)

options.label: B
options.text: They appear as quartets in DEPT-135

options.label: C
options.text: They appear as negative peaks in DEPT-90

questions.correct_answer: They appear in normal 13C broad-band decoupled spectra but disappear in all DEPT spectra (DEPT-45, 90, 135)
questions.explanation: DEPT polarization transfer requires attached hydrogens, leaving quaternary carbons silent.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.topic: 1H NMR trans vs cis alkene coupling constants
questions.question: How do coupling constants (J) distinguish trans-alkene protons from cis-alkene protons?

options.label: B
options.text: trans-Alkenes have large coupling constants (J = 14-18 Hz); cis-alkenes have smaller constants (J = 6-12 Hz)

options.label: C
options.text: trans-Alkenes have J = 2 Hz; cis-alkenes have J = 20 Hz

questions.correct_answer: trans-Alkenes have large coupling constants (J = 14-18 Hz); cis-alkenes have smaller constants (J = 6-12 Hz)
questions.explanation: Vicinal coupling across double bonds is strongly dependent on dihedral angle, being largest for trans coplanar protons.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What is the typical appearance and chemical shift of a carboxylic acid proton (R-COOH) in 1H NMR?

options.label: B
options.text: A very broad, downfield signal at δ 10.0 to 12.5 ppm

options.label: C
options.text: A sharp singlet at δ 2.1 ppm

questions.correct_answer: A very broad, downfield signal at δ 10.0 to 12.5 ppm
questions.explanation: Strong hydrogen bonding and electron withdrawal shift carboxylic acid protons to extreme downfield positions.
